channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Farrukh Abduraimov Elected First Deputy Chairman of Uzbekistan's Supreme Court
item.description: The Senate Council of Uzbekistan has elected Farrukh Abduraimov as the First Deputy Chairman of the Supreme Court for a five-year term. This appointment is part of ongoing reforms aimed at strengthening judicial independence and public trust in the courts. Alisher Usmanov was relieved of his previous position as First Deputy Chairman.

item.title: Orif Bozorov Appointed Deputy Governor of Bukhara Region for Compliance and Anti-Corruption
item.description: Orif Bozorov has been appointed as the Deputy Governor of Bukhara Region, responsible for compliance and internal anti-corruption control. Bozorov, born in 1979, graduated from Tashkent State Law Institute in 2002. Previously, he served as the head of the Tashkent Region Department of the Bureau for Compulsory Enforcement under the Prosecutor General's Office.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Public Debt Approaches $10.4 Billion Mark
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's public debt reached $10.37 billion as of September 30, according to the Ministry of Finance. This figure represents 38.55% of the projected GDP for 2026, a slight decrease from the end of 2025. External debt constitutes 50.9% of the total, with multilateral concessional loans and bilateral concessional loans being the largest components.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Labor and UNICEF Discuss Support for Families Returning from Conflict Zones
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Labor, Social Security, and Migration, along with UNICEF, discussed measures to support citizens and their families returning from conflict zones. Discussions included psychological aid, training for social workers, and ensuring children's access to medical and educational services. Joint regional trips are planned to assess needs and service accessibility.

item.title: Kazakhstan Grants Citizens Control Over Their Pension Savings
item.description: Kazakh citizens have been granted the right to manage their pension contributions. This development allows individuals more agency over their retirement funds. The specifics of the management rights and the implications for the pension system are expected to be detailed further.

item.title: Kazakh-Singaporean Consortium Builds Power Plants in Semey and Ust-Kamenogorsk
item.description: A consortium of Kazakh and Singaporean companies, led by "Atyrau Energo Service," is constructing thermal power plants in Semey and Ust-Kamenogorsk. The project involves equipment supply from Singapore, while "Atyrau Energo Service" handles design and secures bank guarantees. "VD Stroy-Engineering" is also participating in the construction.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Dialogue on President Tokayev's Address Held with Enterprise Workers
item.description: Members of a national outreach group met with employees of the "Kainar-AKB" battery production plant in Taldykorgan to discuss President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address. The importance of manufacturing enterprises for job creation and budget revenue was highlighted. The success of "Kainar-AKB" in foreign markets was noted as a demonstration of domestic production potential.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Shops and Pharmacies as Safe Havens for Domestic Violence Victims
item.description: A proposal in Kazakhstan suggests using local shops and pharmacies as safe points for women and children fleeing domestic violence. The PANA project aims to create a network of easily accessible 'trust points' without requiring government funding. Staff would offer initial assistance and contact emergency services.

item.title: New Airports Under Construction in Zaisan, Kendirli, and Katonkaragay Nearing Completion
item.description: Construction of three new airports in Kazakhstan is nearing completion. The Zaisan and Kendirli airports are expected to be ready by the end of this year, while the Katonkaragay airport project will conclude in February next year. Flights are anticipated to commence in the first half of 2025.

item.title: South Korea to Provide $1.9 Million for Smart Transport Development in Dushanbe
item.description: South Korea will provide $1.9 million to Dushanbe for the development of a smart transport system. This system aims to regulate road conditions, manage traffic flow, and improve public transportation operations. Further details are expected.

item.title: Uzbek President Orders Improved Water Supply and Bus Services in Bukhara
item.description: Uzbek President has ordered the provision of centralized drinking water to 55 neighborhoods in Bukhara. He also directed efforts to accelerate the delivery of an additional 120 buses to the region. Tasks were also set for the education and healthcare sectors.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Build New Oil Refinery with 2 Million Ton Capacity
item.description: Kazakhstan is planning to construct a new oil refinery with an annual processing capacity of 2 million tons. This development aims to enhance the country's oil refining capabilities and potentially reduce reliance on imported refined products.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish National Laboratory for Advanced Materials Research
item.description: Kazakhstan will establish a National Laboratory in Astana to develop advanced materials and reduce import dependency. The lab will identify priority areas for raw material base development and accelerate integration into global production chains. Focus sectors include battery materials, jet engine parts, semiconductors, and permanent magnets. International collaborations are underway.

item.title: East Kazakhstan Region Plans Construction of 25 Major Facilities
item.description: The East Kazakhstan region plans to construct 25 major facilities in the upcoming year. Projects include a multi-profile hospital in Ust-Kamenogorsk, school constructions, and sports facilities like a ski-roller track and an ice palace. Several projects are in development, aiming to boost infrastructure and public services across the region.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Industry Minister Forecasts Car Price Drop by Year-End
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Industry and Construction, Yerbolat Nadyrbayev, predicts a decrease in car prices by the end of the year due to manufacturer discounts and promotions. He noted that domestic car production is increasing, with two new plants expected to boost output. Prices for locally assembled cars have already fallen by 10-11%.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank May Lower Key Rate Below 10% by 2029
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank does not rule out a gradual reduction of the key rate below 10% between 2027 and 2029. This depends on inflation stabilizing at the target 5% and a decrease in public and business inflation expectations. Decisions on monetary policy easing will be based on current inflation dynamics and economic risks.

item.title: Expert Outlines Five Priorities for Implementing Kazakhstan's Presidential Address
item.description: An expert has identified five key priorities for implementing the tasks outlined in President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address. These include interaction between political institutions and civil society, legislative updates, economic development, and strengthening legal culture. The expert emphasized that successful implementation requires active involvement from political institutions, civil society, businesses, and citizens, not just government bodies.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Digital Minister Urges Urgent Measures Against Data Leaks
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Digital Technologies, Sherzod Shermatov, has called for urgent measures to protect personal data following reports of potential leaks. While not confirming specific figures, he warned of risks if immediate action isn't taken, emphasizing the need to invest in cybersecurity alongside AI development. He cited the Binance hack and the 'Butterfly' hacker group's actions as examples of threats.

item.title: Pavlodar School Reports Rape of Students, Police Open Criminal Cases
item.description: Police in the Pavlodar region have opened two criminal cases following reports of the rape of schoolchildren. The police department confirmed the detention of suspects. The investigation is ongoing, and further details are not being disclosed in the interest of the investigation.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Oil Reserves Sufficient for Over 45 Years, Says KazMunayGas
item.description: Kazakhstan's oil reserves are estimated to be sufficient for more than 45 years, according to Askhat Khasenov, Chairman of KazMunayGas. He stated that current reserves stand at 785 million tons, with annual production around 26 million tons. Khasenov emphasized that the resource base is continuously replenished through ongoing exploration activities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Defense Minister Meets Russian Counterpart to Discuss 2027 Cooperation Plans
item.description: Kazakhstan's Defense Minister Aidarbekov met with his Russian counterpart in Astana to discuss military cooperation for 2027, focusing on personnel training and military-technical interaction. Aidarbekov also briefed the Russian minister on Kazakhstan's ongoing army reforms, aimed at enhancing combat readiness, improving military management, and modernizing equipment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Investment Strategies for Pension Fund Contributors
item.description: Kazakhstan's financial market regulator has introduced new investment strategies for pension fund contributors who have transferred their savings to private managers. Contributors can now choose between conservative, moderate, and aggressive risk profiles, allowing for personalized investment approaches based on their proximity to retirement age.

item.title: Kazakhstan Names Partners for First Two Nuclear Power Plants, Targeting 2035 Completion
item.description: Kazakhstan's Energy Minister, Yerlan Akkenzhenov, announced partners for the country's first two nuclear power plants. Russia's Rosatom will collaborate on the "Balkhash" plant, while China National Nuclear Corporation is being considered for the "Moynkum" plant. The minister expressed confidence that projects will be completed by 2035.

item.title: US Midterm Election Results Could Increase Pressure on Biden's Russia, Ukraine, and Iran Policies
item.description: Democratic victories in the US midterm elections are expected to shift the balance of power in Congress, giving Democrats greater oversight and legislative influence. This could impact US policy towards Russia, Ukraine, and Iran. While President Trump stated readiness to work with Democrats, Republican opposition and presidential veto power may limit legislative changes.

item.title: Rising Food Prices in Kabul Leave Low-Income Families Facing Emptier Tables
item.description: Kabul residents are concerned about rising food prices and the increasing cost of living, which is eroding purchasing power. Experts warn of severe humanitarian and economic consequences if the trend continues, making basic needs harder to meet, especially for low-income families. Prices for flour, cooking oil, rice, potatoes, and onions have significantly increased.

item.title: Bukhara Petrochemical Cluster Expected to Receive $420 Million in Investment
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Tekhnochem enterprise in Bukhara region to review plans for expanding its oil and chemical cluster. An investment program for 2024-2028 aims for $420 million, with $200 million already invested. Funding will come from Uzbek and Canadian founders and bank loans.

item.title: Almaty Authorities Identify 2003 Trade Violations, Including Food Price Markups
item.description: Almaty's Department of Entrepreneurship and Investment, along with consumer protection agencies, has identified 2003 violations in trade activities, including excessive markups on essential food items. Over 82 million tenge in fines have been issued to businesses for non-compliance with trade regulations and price limits.

item.title: Kazakhstan Deputy Proposes Stricter Gas Safety Controls After Over 290 Deaths
item.description: A deputy has urged stricter control over gas safety in apartment buildings in Kazakhstan, citing over 290 deaths and 1,337 injuries from carbon monoxide poisoning in the last five years. The issue is particularly concerning in older buildings due to poor ventilation and chimney maintenance. Residents' refusal to sign maintenance contracts exacerbates the problem.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Launch 200 New Production Facilities Worth 1.7 Trillion Tenge by Year-End
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to launch approximately 200 new production facilities with a total value of about 1.7 trillion tenge by the end of the year. This initiative aims to shift the economy from raw material extraction towards processing, reducing import dependency. State support will prioritize projects with significant economic impact.

item.title: Kazakhstan's public debt reaches 38.8 trillion tenge, 20.2% of GDP
item.description: Kazakhstan's public debt has reached 38.8 trillion tenge, equivalent to 20.2% of its GDP, according to Finance Minister Madi Takiev. The ministry projects the debt will not exceed 25% of GDP by 2030. Efforts are underway to reduce the budget deficit by increasing domestic revenue.

item.title: Chinese Premier Li Qiang concludes successful visit to Tajikistan for SCO meeting
item.description: Chinese Premier Li Qiang completed a successful official visit to Tajikistan from October 18-20, attending the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government of the SCO member states. The visit aimed to deepen China-Tajikistan relations and promote high-quality development of the SCO.

item.title: Kazakhstan develops national cargo airline 'Air Cargo' with a fleet of 10 aircraft
item.description: Kazakhstan has established a national cargo airline, 'Air Cargo,' which will eventually operate a fleet of 10 aircraft. The first plane is expected in November 2026. This initiative aims to enhance the country's transit potential and integrate with road and rail networks.

item.title: Public Health Emergency Operations Center Opens in Nukus with US Support
item.description: A Public Health Emergency Operations Center has opened in Nukus, Karakalpakstan, with financial support from the US government and technical assistance from UNICEF. The center aims to strengthen the region's capacity to prepare for and respond to infectious disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies.

item.title: US Court Temporarily Halts Deportation of Over 150 Afghan Migrants
item.description: A federal court in New York has issued a temporary order halting the deportation of more than 150 Afghan migrants. The order, effective until November 7, prevents the transfer of migrants to Afghanistan or Pakistan, as no flights were scheduled by the end of the week.

item.title: Four Killed in Two Separate Traffic Accidents in Afghanistan's Balkh Province
item.description: Four people died and four others were injured in two separate traffic accidents in Balkh province. The Taliban police attributed the accidents to driver negligence. One accident involved a collision between two vehicles, killing three, while a tanker truck and a car collision killed one.

item.title: First SCO Plus Dialogue on Security Issues to Be Held in Samarkand
item.description: The first expert dialogue of the 'SCO Plus on Security Issues' will convene in Samarkand on November 5-6. The meeting, chaired by the head of Uzbekistan's State Security Service, will focus on combating terrorism and extremism in the digital age. Delegations from 24 countries and international organizations are expected to attend.

item.title: Uzbekistan Replaces 'Religious Extremism' with General Term, Eases Penalties
item.description: Uzbekistan has amended its laws on extremism, replacing the term 'religious extremism' with a general 'extremism' to ensure a unified legal approach. The new law, effective November 3, introduces administrative penalties for first-time offenses related to extremist materials and symbols, with criminal liability reserved for repeat violations. Penalties for participation in extremist organizations have also been softened.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Bans Sale of Houses at Foundation Stage, Restricts Advertising
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has prohibited the sale of houses during the foundation stage of construction. Advertising apartments before the initial construction phase is also forbidden. Developers who violate these new regulations will face legal consequences. The new rules aim to protect buyers and ensure project completion.

item.title: Tajikistan and China Discuss Coal Mining and Solar Power Plant Development
item.description: Tajikistan's Energy Minister met with a Chinese delegation to discuss expanding energy cooperation. Key topics included developing coal fields, implementing modern coal technologies, and constructing solar power plants. Both sides expressed readiness to explore joint investment projects and strengthen mutually beneficial collaboration in the energy sector.

item.title: Uzbek President Demands Plan to Raise Incomes for Citizens Working Abroad and Reduce Poverty
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has instructed officials to develop a district-by-district plan to retrain citizens working low-wage jobs abroad and help them find higher-paying employment. The goal is to increase the income of 270,000 citizens to an average or higher level.
